# ZPA create-operation publication and runtime evidence capture

**Captured:** 2026-07-20

This capture records a narrow discrepancy between the live
`automate.zscaler.com` Docusaurus operation inventory, legacy Zscaler Help API
pages, current first-party clients, and authenticated vendor acceptance tests.
It distinguishes operation publication from observed runtime behavior; neither
the legacy Help schemas nor unauthenticated gateway responses establish the
current OneAPI create contract by themselves.

## Sources

- [Configuring App Connector Groups Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-app-connector-groups-using-api)
- [App Connector Management API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/app-connector-management-api)
- [Log Streaming Service (LSS) Configuration](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/log-streaming-service-lss-configuration)
- [Managing Log Streaming Service Configurations Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/managing-log-streaming-service-configurations-using-api)
- [Server Group Management](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/server-group-management) — includes the Private Service Edge Group Management endpoint inventory
- [Terraform provider ZPA acceptance run, 2026-07-20](https://github.com/zscaler/terraform-provider-zpa/actions/runs/29743240346)
- [Go SDK ZPA integration run, 2026-05-24](https://github.com/zscaler/zscaler-sdk-go/actions/runs/26364052234)

## Create operations absent from the live Automate inventory

The 2026-07-20 Docusaurus capture decoded all 1,207 discovered operations with
no decode failures. The following POST operations were present in the prior
capture but absent from the current compiled route inventory. The old App
Connector Group operation URL now returns Automate's Page Not Found view, while
the current category inventories publish collection GET and item
GET/PUT/DELETE operations without the collection POST.

| Resource | Method and path | Help/client evidence | Authenticated runtime evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| App Connector Group | `POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/appConnectorGroup` | Legacy Help and current SDK/provider/Ansible/MCP clients implement create | Confirmed on a OneAPI beta tenant by the 2026-07-20 Terraform acceptance test; a 2026-05-24 production test also reached payload validation |
| LSS configuration | `POST /mgmtconfig/v2/admin/customers/{customerId}/lssConfig` | Legacy Help and current SDK/provider clients implement create | Not currently confirmed: the provider acceptance test is disabled and the latest public Go integration run stopped before LSS |
| Private Service Edge Group | `POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/serviceEdgeGroup` | Help and current first-party clients implement create | Confirmed on a OneAPI beta tenant by the 2026-07-20 Terraform acceptance test |

## Authenticated create evidence

The 2026-07-20 Terraform provider run used the same commit vendored in this
repository (`02c88e27da98ec75f7a7a85f43486b4f0552dfa9`). Its OneAPI beta-tenant
job passed `TestAccResourceAppConnectorGroup_Basic` in 26.50 seconds and
`TestAccResourceServiceEdgeGroup_Basic` in 25.80 seconds. Each acceptance test
performs create, read, update, import, and destroy through the provider
(`vendor/terraform-provider-zpa/zpa/resource_zpa_app_connector_group_test.go:18-66`,
`vendor/terraform-provider-zpa/zpa/resource_zpa_service_edge_group_test.go:18-67`).
The overall workflow failed on unrelated tenant-state prerequisites and entity
limits, so the two named passing tests—not the workflow conclusion—are the
operation evidence.

The 2026-05-24 Go SDK production-tenant run made an authenticated App Connector
Group POST and received `400 missing.mandatory.params`: the API error named
`signingCertId` as null or empty. Current first-party clients expose the wire
field as `enrollmentCertId` (`enrollment_cert_id` in Python-facing interfaces;
`vendor/zscaler-sdk-go/zscaler/zpa/services/appconnectorgroup/zpa_app_connector_group.go:60`).
That response confirms the operation reached create-payload validation on that
production tenant and exposes a requirement missing from the legacy Help field
table. The current Go integration test was repaired on 2026-05-27 to look up
the `Connector` enrollment certificate and send its ID
(`vendor/zscaler-sdk-go/zscaler/zpa/services/appconnectorgroup/zpa_app_connector_group_test.go:21-53`).
The current Terraform provider, Ansible module, and MCP create tool
independently auto-resolve the same certificate when `enrollment_cert_id` is
not configured
(`vendor/terraform-provider-zpa/zpa/resource_zpa_app_connector_group.go:203-207,233-245`,
`vendor/zpacloud-ansible/plugins/modules/zpa_app_connector_groups.py:235-278,466-468`,
`vendor/zscaler-mcp-server/src/zscaler_mcp/tools/zpa/app_connector_groups.py:324-363`).
The base Python SDK accepts that keyword but omits it from the create method's
docstring and example
(`vendor/zscaler-sdk-python/zscaler/zpa/app_connector_groups.py:254-327`).

LSS does not have equivalent current public runtime evidence. Its Terraform
acceptance test is entirely commented out
(`vendor/terraform-provider-zpa/zpa/resource_zpa_lss_config_controller_test.go:1-4`),
and the latest public Go integration run stopped at the App Connector Group
package before reaching LSS. The current Go LSS integration setup also creates
its prerequisite App Connector Group without an enrollment certificate ID
(`vendor/zscaler-sdk-go/zscaler/zpa/services/lssconfigcontroller/zpa_lss_config_controller_test.go:37-60`),
so a future run would need that setup corrected before it could validate LSS
create. This is a test-coverage gap, not evidence that the LSS endpoint was
removed.

## Unauthenticated probes are non-evidence for route existence

Each probe used customer ID `0`, an empty JSON body, and no authorization
header. Both `config.private.zscaler.com` and `api.zsapi.net` returned the same
`401 auth.header.missing` response for GET, POST, OPTIONS, and PATCH against the
documented collection paths and deliberately nonexistent sibling paths. The
gateway therefore authenticates before exposing route or method resolution.
These responses establish only the authentication boundary and cannot support
any claim about endpoint existence, accepted methods, payload fields, or create
behavior.

## Documentation-group moves with stable method/path signatures

Several apparent operation removals are route-key moves inside the Automate
documentation tree rather than API removals:

- Provisioning Key Management operations moved from the
  `provisioning-key-management` documentation group to `nonce`; their methods
  and paths are unchanged.
- The App Connector Group list operation moved from
  `app-connector-group-management` to `app-connector-group`.
- The LSS list operation moved from
  `log-streaming-service-lss-configuration` to `siem-config`.
- The Private Service Edge Group list operation moved from
  `private-service-edge-group-management` to `service-edge-group`.
- Enrollment certificate and version-profile list operations similarly moved
  to new documentation groups without changing their method/path signatures.

## Interpretation boundary

Treat the three missing POST entries as **Automate publication coverage gaps**,
not a uniform claim about API removal. Authenticated acceptance evidence closes
the runtime question for App Connector Group and Private Service Edge Group on
the tested OneAPI beta tenant. It also shows that the App Connector Group create
schema has moved beyond the legacy Help field table. LSS create remains
implemented across first-party clients but lacks a current public authenticated
success. Until the POST operations return to the compiled Automate inventory,
the current capture cannot certify their request-body required flags across
clouds.
